# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_config_docs.py from spendgate.config.schema. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every key of `spendgate.yaml`. Unknown keys are refused, so a typo fails at start. Money is a quoted string such as `"50 EUR"`, never a number. Secrets are never written here: use `env:NAME` or `file:/absolute/path`. Check a file without starting anything: `spendgate check-config --config spendgate.yaml`. A complete example is [`examples/config.yaml`](../examples/config.yaml).

Durations carry their unit in the key name (`*_seconds`). The top-level sections are in the [Config](#config) table; each linked type has its own table below.

## Config

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `server` | [Server](#server) | required | The proxy's listeners and the key pepper. |
| `ledger` | [Ledger](#ledger) | required | Where money state lives, its currency, and hold timing. |
| `fx` | [Fx](#fx) (optional) | unset | Exchange rates into the ledger currency. Required when any catalog entry is in another currency than `ledger.currency`; startup fails without it. |
| `catalog` | [CatalogPaths](#catalogpaths) | see below | Price catalog overrides on top of the bundled catalog. |
| `providers` | map of `openai` or `azure_openai` or `anthropic` or `bedrock` or `google` or `azure_speech` or `elevenlabs` to [Provider](#provider) | `{}` | Connection defaults per provider slug, used by every deployment of that provider unless the deployment overrides them. |
| `models` | map of name to [ModelRoute](#modelroute) | required | Routable model names. Each alias maps to one catalog id and an ordered list of deployments; failover happens only between deployments of that id. |
| `defaults` | [Defaults](#defaults) | see below | Policy defaults for keys and budgets that do not set their own. |
| `fail_open` | [FailOpen](#failopen) | see below | Explicit, named opt-outs from fail-closed behaviour. Every enabled one is logged as a warning at start. |
| `bootstrap` | [Bootstrap](#bootstrap) | see below | Scopes, budgets and keys created at start. Create-only and idempotent: an existing row is never changed by a restart. `serve` creates scopes and budgets only; keys are created by `spendgate migrate --bootstrap`, which prints each new secret once. |
| `anthropic` | [Anthropic](#anthropic) | see below | Request header allowlists for the Anthropic endpoint. |
| `routing` | [Routing](#routing) | see below | Failover and cooldown behaviour across deployments of one model. |
| `alerts` | [Alerts](#alerts) | all unset | Where budget warnings are sent besides the log. Unset: the `spendgate.budget` log lines only. |
| `observability` | [Observability](#observability) | see below | Optional tracing. Prometheus metrics need no setting. |

## Server

Used at `server`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `listen` | `host:port` | required | Data-plane address, `host:port`. |
| `admin` | [AdminServer](#adminserver) (optional) | unset | Optional separate listener for `/admin/v1` and `/metrics`. Without it they share the data port, and `/metrics` then needs an admin key. |
| `max_body_bytes` | positive integer | `26214400` | Largest accepted audio upload (`/v1/audio/transcriptions`, multipart) in bytes (default 25 MiB). Larger requests are refused with `request_too_large` before the body is read in full. |
| `max_json_body_bytes` | positive integer | `4194304` | Largest accepted JSON request body in bytes (default 4 MiB). JSON parses into about 25 times its size in memory, so it has a smaller cap than an upload. Larger requests are refused with `request_too_large` before the body is read. |
| `body_read_timeout_seconds` | positive integer | `30` | Longest a client may take to send its whole request body (default 30). A slower or stalled upload is refused with HTTP 408 and frees its place at once. |
| `max_request_seconds` | positive integer | `900` | Longest one call or stream may run, end to end (default 900). At the limit the gateway stops it and settles it as `timeout` (buffered) or `stream_broken` (stream): the actual usage if seen, else the full hold. |
| `max_concurrent_requests` | positive integer | `128` | Most requests being admitted at once; beyond it the proxy refuses fast. It covers intake only: a running stream is limited by the key's concurrency. |
| `keep_alive_seconds` | positive integer | `75` | How long an idle client connection stays open (default 75). Keep it above the load balancer's idle timeout (60 s on many), or the balancer may send a request on a connection the proxy is closing and answer it with a 502. |
| `graceful_shutdown_seconds` | positive integer | `30` | Drain deadline after `SIGTERM` (default 30): calls still running then are stopped and settled as cancelled (the full hold once sent, unless usage was seen). Keep it below the orchestrator's grace period minus any `preStop` wait; set it above `max_request_seconds` to let every call finish. See the operations guide, Draining on restart. |
| `key_pepper` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) | required | Secret used to hash stored key secrets: at least 16 bytes (`openssl rand -hex 32`), or the configuration is refused. Keep it: changing it invalidates every key. |

## Ledger

Used at `ledger`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `backend` | [SqliteLedger](#sqliteledger) or [PostgresLedger](#postgresledger) | required | `sqlite` (one host) or `postgres` (shared use); see the two tables below. |
| `currency` | currency code | required | ISO 4217 code of every budget and every recorded cost. |
| `lease_seconds` | positive integer | `60` | How long a hold lives without a heartbeat. A hold whose owner died is charged in full by the sweeper after this time. |
| `heartbeat_seconds` | positive integer (optional) | unset | How often a running call renews its hold. Default is `lease_seconds / 3`; it must be shorter than `lease_seconds`. |
| `sweep_seconds` | positive integer | `30` | How often the server charges and releases expired holds. |
| `retention_days` | positive integer | `90` | Calls older than this many whole UTC days are deleted once a day. Usage reports cover only this window. |
| `auto_migrate` | boolean (optional) | unset | Whether `serve` applies pending migrations at start. Unset means `true` for SQLite (one file on one host) and `false` for Postgres. When false, `serve` refuses a schema that is behind and says to run `spendgate migrate` (or `serve --migrate`): see [upgrades](operations.md#upgrades-and-rollbacks). |
| `pool_min` | integer | `1` | Postgres only: connections each instance keeps open (default 1). Not used by SQLite. |
| `pool_max` | positive integer | `10` | Postgres only: most connections each instance opens (default 10). Size the server's `max_connections` for this times the number of instances, plus migrations and admin. |
| `pool_timeout_seconds` | positive integer | `10` | Postgres only: how long a call waits for a free pooled connection (default 10) before it is refused with `ledger_unavailable`. |

## Fx

Used at `fx`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rates` | map of currency code to quoted decimal | required | Map from currency code to rate: 1 unit of that currency equals this many ledger units, as a quoted decimal such as `"0.92"`. |
| `as_of` | date `YYYY-MM-DD` | required | Date of the rate, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Recorded with every call. |
| `source` | string | required | Where the rate came from, for the audit trail. |

## CatalogPaths

Used at `catalog`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `paths` | list of string | `[]` | Override files in the catalog format, applied in order after the bundled catalog. An entry replaces the bundled one with the same id and `effective_from`. |

## Provider

Used at `providers.<name>`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | string (optional) | unset | Provider API root. `https` only, or `http` for loopback. May be `env:NAME`, read at start. For `openai` and `azure_openai` the upstream must honour `max_completion_tokens`: the proxy sends the held output ceiling in that field only, so an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, LiteLLM, ...) that ignores it does not enforce the ceiling (protocol.md 2.1). |
| `auth` | `api_key` or `bearer_token` or `sigv4` | `"api_key"` | How the proxy authenticates to the provider. |
| `credential` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) or `adc` (optional) | unset | Secret reference for the key or token. Not used with `sigv4`, which reads the standard AWS credential chain. For Vertex AI (`google` with `bearer_token`) it is the service-account JSON, or `adc` for application default credentials (workload identity, the metadata server). A `file:` credential is read again on `SIGHUP`. |
| `region` | string (optional) | unset | Provider region, where the adapter needs one (Bedrock, Azure, Vertex AI). Also selects a catalog entry scoped to this Region (`regions`), if there is one. A Vertex AI deployment (`google` with `bearer_token`) must use a Region an entry of its id lists: it never takes the region-less (Gemini API) price, and is refused at start otherwise. |
| `api_version` | string (optional) | unset | Azure OpenAI query version; leave unset for the v1 path (recommended). A classic version must accept `max_completion_tokens`, the only output ceiling field the proxy sends; the minimum version is not verified here, so prefer the v1 API. |

## ModelRoute

Used at `models.<name>`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `catalog_id` | catalog id `provider/model` | required | Catalog id, `provider/model`. One price entry prices every deployment; no entry in force means `model_not_priced`. Deployments whose Regions resolve to different entries are refused at start: route them as separate models. A route with a Vertex AI deployment is priced only by entries that list its Regions. |
| `deployments` | list of [DeploymentSpec](#deploymentspec) | required | Candidates in preference order. A throttled or unreachable one is skipped for the next, at no cost. |

## Defaults

Used at `defaults`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limits` | [DefaultLimits](#defaultlimits) | see below | Applied to a key for each limit the key does not set itself. |
| `max_output_tokens` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Output ceiling for keys with none of their own. If a request, the key and this all leave it open, the catalog entry's `limits.max_output_tokens` applies. |
| `max_embedding_items` | positive integer | `256` | Most inputs accepted in one embeddings request. |
| `strict_overrun` | boolean | `true` | When a settlement exceeds the hold and breaches the cap, block the budget until an operator runs `budgets ack-overrun`. A budget can override this. |

## FailOpen

Used at `fail_open`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_remote_media` | boolean | `false` | Accept `http(s)` URLs in image positions of request bodies. The provider fetches them itself and treats them as images; spendgate does not fetch or check what they serve, and the fetch is a server-side request forgery risk. Off by default: only inline `data:` URLs are accepted. Inline media must be a png, jpeg, webp or gif image either way: other types are not priced and are refused. |

## Bootstrap

Used at `bootstrap`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scopes` | list of scope path | `[]` | Scope paths to create, for example `org:acme/project:app`. |
| `budgets` | list of [BootstrapBudget](#bootstrapbudget) | `[]` | Budgets to create. Each scope on the path must exist or be listed. |
| `keys` | list of [BootstrapKey](#bootstrapkey) | `[]` | Keys to create: data keys for apps, admin keys for operators. |

## Anthropic

Used at `anthropic`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed_versions` | list of string | `["2023-06-01", "2026-10-21"]` | `anthropic-version` header values the proxy accepts. |
| `allowed_betas` | list of string | `[]` | `anthropic-beta` header values the proxy accepts. Empty: none. |

## Routing

Used at `routing`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_attempts` | positive integer | `2` | Most deployments tried for one request. |
| `cooldown_seconds` | positive integer | `5` | How long a deployment is skipped after its circuit breaker opens, or after the provider answers 429 for a quota or billing reason or with an unreadable `Retry-After`. A busy 429 cools it for its `Retry-After` as given (seconds or an HTTP-date), or without one for a random 250 to 500 ms, doubled for each 429 in a row up to this value; a call that finds every deployment cooling waits up to 1 s for one to come back. A connect failure alone does not cool a deployment. Must not exceed `max_cooldown_seconds`. |
| `failure_threshold_pct` | integer 1 to 100 | `50` | Failure percentage in the window that puts a deployment into cooldown. |
| `min_requests` | positive integer | `5` | Requests in the window before the failure percentage counts. |
| `window_seconds` | positive integer | `60` | Length of the failure window. |
| `max_cooldown_seconds` | positive integer | `300` | Upper bound on any cooldown. |
| `connect_timeout_seconds` | positive integer | `10` | How long to wait for the TCP/TLS connection to the provider (DNS included) before the attempt counts as unreachable. Read and total timeouts are not affected. |

## Alerts

Used at `alerts`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webhook` | [AlertWebhook](#alertwebhook) (optional) | unset | Post each budget warning (`soft_threshold`, `cap_breached`, `blocked`) to one HTTPS endpoint, signed. Used by `spendgate serve` only; library mode logs them. See [budget warnings](operations.md#budget-warning-webhook). |

## Observability

Used at `observability`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `otel` | [Otel](#otel) | see below | OpenTelemetry tracing of the hold, forward and settle steps. |

## AdminServer

Used at `server.admin`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `listen` | `host:port` | required | Admin address, `host:port`. Keep it on loopback or an internal network. The host is bound as given: an address, or a name resolved once at start (in Compose, a network alias such as `spendgate-admin`, so it listens on that one network). `0.0.0.0` binds every interface, including the one apps reach. |

## SqliteLedger

Used at `ledger.backend`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `sqlite` | required | Always `sqlite`. |
| `path` | string | required | Database file. A relative path is relative to the config file. The file must be mode 0600 and is created that way. |

## PostgresLedger

Used at `ledger.backend`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `postgres` | required | Always `postgres`. Needs the `postgres` extra. |
| `dsn` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) | required | Secret reference to the connection URL, password included. Use `sslmode=verify-full` when the server is on another host. Each connection gets lock, statement and idle-in-transaction timeouts plus TCP keepalives and a TCP user timeout unless the URL or the server sets them: see [Postgres connections](operations.md#postgres-connections). A `file:` DSN is read again on `SIGHUP`; only its password may change there. |
| `auth` | [RdsIamAuth](#rdsiamauth) or [EntraAuth](#entraauth) or [CloudSqlIamAuth](#cloudsqliamauth) (optional) | unset | Sign in with a short-lived token from the host's cloud identity instead of a password; the DSN then names the user and carries no password. See [cloud identity](operations.md#cloud-identity-for-the-database). |

## DeploymentSpec

Used at `models.<name>.deployments[]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `openai` or `azure_openai` or `anthropic` or `bedrock` or `google` or `azure_speech` or `elevenlabs` | required | Provider slug. It must match the provider part of `catalog_id`. |
| `model` | string (optional) | unset | The provider's own model or deployment name. Default: the model part of `catalog_id`. |
| `base_url` | string (optional) | unset | Overrides `providers.<slug>.base_url` for this deployment. May be `env:NAME`. |
| `auth` | `api_key` or `bearer_token` or `sigv4` (optional) | unset | Overrides `providers.<slug>.auth` for this deployment. |
| `credential` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) or `adc` (optional) | unset | Overrides `providers.<slug>.credential` for this deployment. |
| `region` | string (optional) | unset | Overrides `providers.<slug>.region` for this deployment, including for pricing. |
| `api_version` | string (optional) | unset | Overrides `providers.<slug>.api_version` for this deployment. |

## DefaultLimits

Used at `defaults.limits`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rpm` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Requests per minute for keys with none of their own. Unset: no limit. |
| `tpm` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Estimated tokens per minute for keys with none of their own. Unset: no limit. The estimate is the worst case, as for a key's own `tpm`. |
| `concurrency` | positive integer (optional) | `16` | Calls in flight at once, per key, for keys with none of their own. It also bounds the overrun at a cap crossing (see how-money-is-protected.md). `null` removes the bound. |

## BootstrapBudget

Used at `bootstrap.budgets[]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | name | required | Stable name; stored as `bootstrap-<id>`. Never recreated once seen. |
| `scope` | scope path | required | Scope path the budget applies to. It must be in `bootstrap.scopes`. |
| `period` | `none` or `day` or `month` | required | `none` is a lifetime cap; `day` and `month` reset at UTC. |
| `cap` | money string such as `"50 USD"` | required | Quoted amount in the ledger currency, such as `"50 EUR"`. |
| `soft_pct` | integer 1 to 99 | `80` | Percentage of the cap that raises a warning, never a refusal. |
| `model_filter` | string (optional) | unset | Apply the budget only to calls whose catalog id (`provider/model`, not the alias) matches this case-sensitive glob, such as `openai/gpt-6-*`. `check-config` and `serve` warn when it matches no routed catalog id. |
| `strict_overrun` | boolean (optional) | unset | Overrides `defaults.strict_overrun` for this budget. |

## BootstrapKey

Used at `bootstrap.keys[]`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | name | required | Label of the key. A name already in use is left alone. |
| `scope` | scope path (optional) | unset | Scope path of a data key. Give this or `admin_scopes`, not both. |
| `admin_scopes` | list of `usage:read` or `keys:write` or `budgets:write` (optional) | unset | Makes an admin key with these permissions. Give this or `scope`. |
| `models` | list of string (optional) | unset | Allow list of aliases or catalog ids. Unset: every routed model. |
| `limits` | [Limits](#limits) | all unset | Rate and concurrency limits of this key. |
| `max_output_tokens` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Output ceiling of this key. |
| `session_defaults` | [SessionDefaultsSpec](#sessiondefaultsspec) (optional) | unset | Limits for sessions on this key. A request that names a session needs them. |
| `session_required` | boolean | `false` | Refuse every call on this key that does not send `X-Spendgate-Session` (`invalid_request`), so an agent cannot leave its session limits behind. Needs `session_defaults`. Like every key setting it applies when the key is created; use `PATCH /admin/v1/keys/{key_id}` for existing keys (`migrate --bootstrap` warns when an existing key differs). |

## AlertWebhook

Used at `alerts.webhook`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) | required | Secret reference to the receiver URL (it often carries a token). `https` only, or `http` for loopback; redirects are not followed. |
| `signing_secret` | secret reference (`env:NAME` or `file:/path`) | required | Secret reference to the HMAC-SHA256 key (UTF-8 text; its UTF-8 bytes are the key). Each post carries `X-Spendgate-Signature: sha256=<hex>` over the exact body bytes. |
| `timeout_seconds` | positive integer | `5` | Longest one delivery attempt may take, end to end. |
| `max_attempts` | integer 1 to 10 | `5` | Tries per warning. A network error, a timeout, a 429 or a 5xx is retried after 1, 2, 4, ... seconds (at most 30); any other answer outside 2xx is final. |
| `queue_size` | integer 1 to 100000 | `1000` | Warnings waiting to be posted. When full, a new warning is dropped and counted in `spendgate_alert_webhooks_total{result="dropped"}`; calls are never delayed. |

## Otel

Used at `observability.otel`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | boolean | `false` | Export one span per hold, forward and settle over OTLP/HTTP, and pass the caller's `traceparent` on to the provider. Needs the `otel` extra (`spendgate[otel]`); without it `serve` warns at start and traces nothing. The exporter reads the standard `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` variables. |
| `service_name` | string | `"spendgate"` | The `service.name` resource attribute of every span. |

## RdsIamAuth

Used at `ledger.backend.auth`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `rds_iam` | required | `rds_iam`: an Amazon RDS or Aurora IAM auth token, signed with the standard AWS credential chain. Needs the `bedrock` extra (botocore). |
| `region` | region name (optional) | unset | AWS region of the database. Default: the AWS chain's region. |

## EntraAuth

Used at `ledger.backend.auth`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `entra` | required | `entra`: a Microsoft Entra ID token from `DefaultAzureCredential` (managed or workload identity, environment) for Azure Database for PostgreSQL. Needs the `azure` extra. |
| `scope` | string | `"https://ossrdbms-aad.database.windows.net/.default"` | Token audience. The default is the one Azure documents for PostgreSQL. |

## CloudSqlIamAuth

Used at `ledger.backend.auth`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `cloudsql_iam` | required | `cloudsql_iam`: a Google access token from application default credentials, for Cloud SQL IAM database sign-in. Needs the `google` extra. |

## Limits

Used at `bootstrap.keys[].limits`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rpm` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Requests per minute. Unset means the `defaults.limits.rpm` value applies. |
| `tpm` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Estimated tokens per minute. Unset means the `defaults.limits.tpm` value applies. The estimate is the worst case: each image counts at the model's image ceiling, up to 61,000 tokens on a model without a documented one. |
| `concurrency` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Calls in flight at once. Unset means the `defaults.limits.concurrency` value applies. |

## SessionDefaultsSpec

Used at `bootstrap.keys[].session_defaults`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `budget` | money string such as `"50 USD"` (optional) | unset | Cap of one session, inside the shared budgets. It only narrows them: a key whose scope chain has no other budget is refused (`no_budget`) even when its sessions have a budget ([ADR-0030](adr/0030-session-budgets-only-narrow.md)). |
| `max_steps` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Most requests in one session. |
| `max_seconds` | positive integer (optional) | unset | Wall-clock limit from the first call of a session. |
| `idle_seconds` | positive integer (optional) | unset | A session idle this long is closed and the same id starts a fresh one. |
| `max_new_sessions_per_hour` | positive integer (optional) | `60` | Most new sessions this key may start in an hour, idle restarts included, so minting session ids cannot dodge the limits. `null` removes the bound. |
